text:
incident-bot: PAGER: inference-runtime p95 latency spike + error-rate increase affecting hosted text-gen and embeddings. Auto-escalate to primary oncall @ana and secondary @leo. Attachments: error samples, sample traces.

ana: typo: I'm ana. Saw this at ~09:50 UTC. Dashboards show a simultaneous drop in kv_cache_hit_ratio from ~96% -> ~55% and a surge in worker restarts. p95 for text-gen up from ~130ms -> ~900ms.

leo: confirming. I'm seeing fallback_quant_kernel logs right after "kv_cache_eviction: true" events. Several workers hit OOM and retried. This looks like a mem-pressure cascade.

maria: we shipped an ML infra tweak last night to enable denser int8 packing for the LLM attention kernels. Canary passed basic perf tests but maybe not these long-prefix workloads.

ops-bot: Pager acknowledged. Creating mitigation job slot.

sre_lead: immediate plan: 1) throttle batch size and reduce batch window for affected pools (owner: @ana), 2) flip feature flag for new quant profile to off on canary (owner: @devon), 3) disable prefix KV caching for worst-hit shards (owner: @maria), 4) notify CS for impacted customers (owner: @kate-cs). If mitigation not stable in 30m, escalate rollback to prod.

ana: reducing batch size for model rwd/long-v2: max_batch_size 64 -> 8 and batch_window_ms 50 -> 10. Command:```bash
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/runtime/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd/long-v2","max_batch_size":8,"batch_window_ms":10}'
```

ops-bot: runtime-config-update job queued id rc-12007 by ana.

maria: disabling prefix cache on shards s-03 and s-07 (canary). Doing one shard at a time.

kate-cs: CS update: we've got 4 tickets complaining about slowness for embeddings. Two are high-volume customers (enterprise tier). I've emailed account reps and opened a short-hold comms.

ben: logs: pattern is eviction -> cache_miss -> quant_fallback -> increased resident set -> more evictions. Sequence lengths for affected requests are longer than average but within expected distribution.

leo: I recommend running the quant rollback on canary first. Devon, can you stage the flip?

devon: prepared flag flip: FEATURE_TOGGLES: ENABLE_DENSE_INT8=false. Tested in staging. Rollout playbook: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 5m health checks. ETA ~8m to complete.

ops-bot: feature-flip rollout started ff-12007 by devon.

incident-bot: logged initial incident note and created a ticket in #incidents.

maria: after disabling caching on s-03, hit ratio improved from 58% -> 80% in 7 minutes, and canary p95 dropped from 880ms -> 260ms.

ana: after reducing batch params and starting the rollout, worker OOMs dropped immediately. Canary traces look stable.

ops-bot: rollout healthchecks green at 25%. Promoting to 100%.

devon: rollback to disable dense int8 completed at 10:12 UTC across fleet. Monitoring.

leo: post-rollback, p95 for affected endpoints trending back to normal ~140ms, error-rate returning to baseline. No new OOMs in last 15 minutes.

kate-cs: informed customers that mitigation is in place and were doing an RCA. Customers asked for ETA on RCA; I provided 48 hours for a draft.

sre_lead: incident status -> mitigated. Please plan postmortem. Ana, schedule a postmortem meeting and owner a doc.

ana: scheduling postmortem for tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Invite: @devon, @maria, @leo, @sre_lead, @kate-cs, @ben, platform-qa.

ben: initial RCA hypothesis: dense int8 packing increases transient memory per-request on the GPU kernels; when combined with aggressive batching and a pre-existing small bug in eviction thresholding, it caused eviction storms that cascaded to fallback kernels and worker restarts. Two contributing factors: rollout gating lacked long-prefix synthetic workloads and there was no alert for rapid kv cache collapse.

maria: will export shard-level eviction traces and KV metrics, include a list of affected shard IDs and timestamps.

devon: will add a CI check that runs quant profile changes against synthetic long-prefix scenarios and verifies p95 token latency. If regression >5% block the merge.

sre_lead: action items (add to remediation tracker and assign):
- ACTION-101: Add preflight synthetic workload tests for quant changes (owner: ml-infra / @devon). Block merges on >5% p95 regression.
- ACTION-102: Add alert rule and paging for kv cache hit-rate drops (>15% delta in 5m) with automatic tagging of affected shards (owner: @maria). Suggested promql:
  delta(kv_cache_hit_ratio[5m]) < -0.15 and increase(kv_cache_evictions[5m]) > 50
- ACTION-103: Add runtime safety interlock: if worker mem usage > 80% or OOM_count > 0 for 2m -> auto-reduce max_batch_size by 50% (owner: runtime-team / @ana). Short-term rule to implement in infra.
- ACTION-104: Add canary workload that replays long-prefix sequences during release gating (owner: platform-qa / @ben).
- ACTION-105: Update deployment runbook with explicit quant rollback steps and customer-comm templates (owner: @kate-cs).

ana: quick short-term note: I'll push a hotfix to infra to auto-shrink batch size on OOM > 0 for 2m. PR will include config knobs.

devon: adding per-model perf benchmarks into CI and a synthetic suite for attention-heavy workloads.

maria: drafting alert query and dashboard panels for shard-level hit rate, eviction spikes, and fallback kernel counts.

ben: I'll own synthetic canary tests and include them in the next release pipeline. Test plan: 10k long-prefix requests with reproducible token distribution and burst patterns.

sre_lead: timeline: postmortem doc draft by EOD tomorrow, action items entered into the tracker by EOD+2, follow-up in 14 days to validate mitigations.

kate-cs: will prepare customer impact summary and comms language once postmortem draft exists.

ops-bot: reminder set for postmortem in 24h. Incident channel will be updated with the postmortem link when available.

ana: handing back to normal ops. I'll post a concise summary and link to the postmortem doc in #incidents once it's live. Thanks team. :thanks: 

leo: tagging next oncall @sre_lead to track follow-ups.

sre_lead: acknowledged. I'll make sure action items are triaged and owners report progress. Good work everyone.
